title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - General Objectives of Social Studies
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: One of the fundamental objectives of Social Studies is to develop the learner's ability to do which of the following?
options: Avoid interacting with culturally different groups
Memorize ancient European political history verbatim
Adapt successfully to a constantly changing environment
Overthrow traditional and democratic systems of government
questions.explain: A central objective of the subject is equipping students with the critical thinking and problem-solving skills needed to **adapt to their changing physical and social environment**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When a curriculum aims to inculcate a deep sense of loyalty, pride, and belonging to one's country, it is promoting:
options: Nepotism and tribalism
National consciousness and patriotism
Ethnocentrism and bias
Global isolationism
questions.explain: **National consciousness** refers to an individual's awareness of belonging to a nation, which breeds patriotism and a collective desire to see the nation succeed.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: According to the general objectives of Social Studies, which description best defines a "good citizen"?
options: An individual capable of and willing to contribute to societal development
A person who focuses exclusively on acquiring personal wealth
Someone who refuses to participate in democratic civic duties
A citizen who relies entirely on the government for basic survival
questions.explain: Social Studies defines a good citizen not merely as a resident of a country, but as someone **active, capable, and willing to contribute positively** to the development of the society.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the "right types of values and attitudes" that Social Studies seeks to inculcate in youths?
options: Apathy towards communal issues
Honesty, tolerance, and hard work
Intolerance and greed
Disrespect for constitutional authority
questions.explain: The "right values" include positive virtues such as **honesty, tolerance, hard work, and respect**, which are necessary for peaceful coexistence and progress.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Developing a student's problem-solving skills to collaboratively tackle community challenges directly fulfills which objective of Social Studies?
options: Promoting religious supremacy in the region
Contributing to the practical development of the society
Isolating local communities from modern technological advances
Encouraging a sedentary lifestyle among youths
questions.explain: Equipping students with problem-solving skills empowers them to identify issues within their communities and take proactive steps, fulfilling the objective of **contributing to societal development**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: By teaching learners about the mutual interdependence of different ethnic and religious groups, Social Studies actively attempts to eliminate:
options: Ethnic bigotry and societal conflicts
Economic development and trade
Democratic governance processes
National unity and patriotism
questions.explain: Highlighting interdependence helps individuals appreciate diversity, thereby reducing **ethnic bigotry, stereotypes, and conflicts**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If a student respectfully recites the National Anthem and protects public infrastructure, they are demonstrating which core objective of the subject?
options: Civic disobedience
Academic manipulation
National consciousness and citizenship
Traditional dominance
questions.explain: Respecting national symbols (like the anthem) and protecting public property are practical demonstrations of **national consciousness and responsible citizenship**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Why is the continuous inculcation of positive values emphasized as a fundamental objective for basic education learners?
options: To replace indigenous languages with a uniform foreign language
To enable youths to function effectively as responsible moral agents in society
To prepare students exclusively for immediate migration to foreign nations
To force all citizens to adhere to a single global religion
questions.explain: The ultimate aim of value-based education is the molding of character. It enables learners to grow into adults who function effectively and responsibly as **moral agents** in their society.
